issues.description: Per-frame AWS client creation defeats connection reuse and adds nontrivial constant overhead
issues.detail: Every LLMContextFrame creates a fresh `aioboto3.Session().client("bedrock-agentcore", ...)` inside an `async with`. Client construction is not free: it loads service models, parses endpoints, and establishes TLS on first use. If the processor is invoked repeatedly in a streaming voice loop, this constant factor will dominate latency for short responses. The asymptotic complexity per invocation is fine (O(n) in response bytes), but the constants are paying interest the profiler would call out. A long-lived client created once at startup (and torn down on cleanup) is the right data-structure-of-state here.

issues.description: Timeout-close task uses `asyncio.sleep` plus a state flag without a documented invariant; race window on rapid frame arrival
issues.detail: The `_close_output_response_after_timeout` coroutine sleeps 1.0s then closes if `_output_response_open` is still set. The cancellation is done by awaiting `cancel_task` in `_push_text_frame`, but there is no stated loop/state invariant tying `_close_task`, `_output_response_open`, and `_last_text_frame_time` together. The variable `_last_text_frame_time` is written but never read, suggesting the design started as a deadline check and devolved into a fire-and-forget timer; the dead field is a tell. State the invariant explicitly (e.g. "_output_response_open is true iff a Start has been pushed and no End has yet been pushed; _close_task is None or a pending task that will push End unless cancelled before sleep completes"), then either use the deadline field or delete it. As written, a careful reader cannot follow this without running it.

issues.description: SSE line parsing is incorrect for multi-line `data:` events and silently drops `event:`/comment lines
issues.detail: The multi-part branch splits on `\n` and rejects any line not starting with `data: `. Real Server-Sent Events permit multi-line `data:` continuations (concatenated with `\n`), `event:`, `id:`, `retry:` fields, and comment lines beginning with `:`. The current code logs a warning and drops them, then treats each `data:` line as an independent JSON response. If AgentCore ever emits a chunked JSON payload across two `data:` lines (legitimate per spec), parsing will fail mid-stream. Either restrict the contract in the docstring ("we assume one JSON object per data line, no continuations, no event types") or implement the SSE state machine. State the invariant being relied on.

issues.description: `default_response_to_output_transformer` lets `json.JSONDecodeError` propagate, killing the stream on a single malformed line
issues.detail: If any line is not valid JSON (e.g. a heartbeat, a partial chunk from an SSE continuation, or a server hiccup), the exception unwinds out of the `async for` loop and the entire response is lost, including any text already buffered before the close-bookend logic runs. Correctness here is not the same as testedness: a proved-correct happy path is not a robust default transformer. Catch the decode error and log+skip, or document loudly that any malformed line terminates the response.

issues.description: Public parameter `agentArn` violates PEP 8 and the surrounding module's snake_case convention
issues.detail: Every other parameter on `__init__` is snake_case (`aws_access_key`, `context_to_payload_transformer`). `agentArn` is camelCase, presumably mirroring the AWS API field `agentRuntimeArn`. This is a small readability nit, but library code is exactly where Knuth's "write for the reader" applies: a Python user will reach for `agent_arn` by reflex. Rename to `agent_arn` (the internal attribute `_agentArn` likewise) and pass `agentRuntimeArn=self._agent_arn` at the boundary where AWS naming is required.

issues.description: `default_context_to_payload_transformer` joins list-content with a space without separating between text parts that already contain spaces, and silently drops non-text parts
issues.detail: `prompt = " ".join([part.get("text", "") for part in content])` will insert an extra space for every non-text part (image, tool_use, etc.), since they contribute `""` to the join. For a content list of length k with j text parts, the result has k-1 spaces regardless of j; the invariant "prompt is the concatenation of text parts separated by single spaces" does not hold. Filter to parts that actually have text, or document the simplification.

issues.description: Magic constant `1.0` for response timeout is undocumented and unmeasured
issues.detail: `self._output_response_timeout = 1.0` is hardcoded inside `__init__` with no comment, no constructor parameter, and no measurement justifying the value. For voice pipelines where end-of-response latency directly affects perceived turn-taking, 1.0s is a long time to wait before closing a response that already ended. Either expose it as a parameter or comment what it's tuned against. "Don't optimize without measuring" cuts both ways: don't pick a constant without justifying it either.

issues.description: `line[6:]` magic slice and string contract not lifted to a named constant
issues.detail: `line = line[6:]  # omit "data: "` repeats the literal `"data: "` semantics in two places (the startswith check and the slice). Replace with `prefix = "data: "; line = line.removeprefix(prefix)` or at least `len(prefix)`. Small nit, but exactly the kind of off-by-one a careful reader has to verify by counting characters.

issues.description: Module docstring names a class that does not exist
issues.detail: The file docstring says "This module defines the AWSAgentCoreProcessor" but the PR title and class are `AWSBedrockAgentCoreProcessor` / `AWSAgentCoreProcessor` depending on where you look. Reconcile the names; the docstring is the first thing a literate reader sees.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED with NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT for the bookend state machine. The core algorithm (transform context, invoke, stream parts, emit text frames) is straightforward and the asymptotic complexity is fine, but the invariants that hold the streaming state together (`_output_response_open`, `_close_task`, the orphaned `_last_text_frame_time`) are not stated anywhere, and a reader cannot verify correctness without simulating execution. The SSE parser is a narrow happy-path implementation that silently drops valid-by-spec lines and dies on a single malformed JSON. Per-invocation AWS client creation is a constant-factor cost that a profiler would flag immediately in a voice loop; this is the 3% worth optimizing. Smaller readability nits (camelCase `agentArn`, magic 1.0 timeout, magic `[6:]` slice, docstring naming the wrong class) are easy fixes that compound into library-grade clarity.
